name: Teri Okafor
life: Teri still has the envelope containing the first rejection from a packaging firm. She'd printed sample boxes that wasted a strip of card. What an accountant calls waste has often been the part people remember. Tuesday often includes a stop at the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, where Teri checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: The thirteenth slot was a cutting mistake I was ashamed of. I'm taking the old die to the design school with a box full of people's notes and a copy of the rejected invoice.
appearance: Teri is easy to recognize by a long plait tucked inside the collar and a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Usually dressed in a mustard canvas overshirt with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light, Teri grins on one side while the eyes stay serious when listening.
personality: Teri enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
agenda: To show the cutting mistake to students together with the actual box.
family: Owen Green is Teri’s cousin. Teri brings a spare shopping bag. Owen chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *A summer marriage*, Owen says, “I am their oldest friend. My speech is mostly about the groom's ex and I'm rewriting every line.”
connections: Nora Reiss. The packaging error cannot become a bank forecast until someone decides whether the thirteenth slot is for sale.
